chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Idris and others, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Jamilah, from Zayd al-Shahham, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

In zakat, one may give from it to the brother, the sister, the paternal uncle, the paternal aunt, the maternal uncle, and the maternal aunt, but one does not give to the grandfather or the grandmother.

As for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Imran ibn Ismail ibn Imran al-Qummi, who said: I wrote to Abu al-Hasan al-Thani (peace be upon him) saying, 'I have children, men and women; is it permissible for me to give them from zakat?' He wrote back (peace be upon him): 'That is permissible for you.' This report is specific to him. Do you not see that when he said 'That is permissible for you,' he attached the permissibility to him alone, not others, even though it is possible that he only permitted him this due to the smallness of his wealth, and that it would not suffice for what he needs for the maintenance of his dependents, so he allowed him to make his zakat an addition to the maintenance of his dependents. And this is permissible if the matter is as we mentioned, and that which indicates this is what was narrated:

key_terms.الْخَالُ وَالْخَالَةُ: The maternal uncle and maternal aunt
key_terms.الْعَمُّ وَالْعَمَّةُ: The paternal uncle and paternal aunt

ai.seo_question: Can a Muslim give zakat to their parents, grandparents, or children?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *nasab* (lineage) and *qaraba* (kinship) in zakat distribution, permitting gifts to siblings and collateral relatives while excluding direct ascendants like grandparents to avoid double benefit. The secondary report regarding children is interpreted by scholars as a specific concession (*khass*) for those with limited wealth, allowing zakat to supplement rather than replace obligatory maintenance (*nafaqah*). This reflects the Shia juristic principle that one cannot give zakat to those whom one is already financially obligated to support, such as parents and children, unless the obligation is not fully met.
